identity_held_roles.title: Director of Quality & Compliance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Reports to:** Executive Director

 

**Job Summary:**

The Director of Quality and Compliance for the PACE (Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) Program will oversee and manage all aspects of quality assurance, compliance, and regulatory adherence for the PACE program. This role ensures that the program operates in full compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, as well as upholds the highest standards of care for the elderly participants. The Director will lead efforts to continuously improve program quality, enhance participant satisfaction, and drive performance excellence across the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

1. Regulatory Compliance Management:

* Ensure adherence to all PACE-related federal, state, and local regulations, including CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) and state-specific requirements.

* Monitor and interpret updates to regulatory policies, and adjust organizational practices as necessary to remain compliant.

* Act as the primary liaison between the organization and regulatory agencies, ensuring timely reporting and response to audits, surveys, and inspections.

2. Quality Assurance and Improvement:

* In collaboration with the Medical Director develop, implement, and evaluate quality improvement initiatives to ensure high standards of care, safety, and service delivery for participants.

* Collaborate with clinical and operational teams to analyze performance metrics and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

* Oversee the development and execution of corrective action plans (CAPs) for any areas of deficiency, ensuring timely resolution.

3. Risk Management and Reporting:

* Lead risk assessment processes to identify potential compliance and quality issues, minimizing risk to the organization and participants.

* Develop and implement risk mitigation strategies, including monitoring trends, identifying patterns, and taking proactive actions.

* Ensure the organization is prepared for external audits and inspections, managing all compliance-related documentation and reporting.

4. Staff Training and Development:

* Develop and conduct ongoing training programs for staff on compliance, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

* Foster a culture of compliance and continuous improvement across the organization by leading educational initiatives and creating awareness.

* Provide guidance and support to staff on regulatory changes, quality standards, and best practices.

5. Participant Care and Satisfaction:

* Advocate for participants’ safety and satisfaction, ensuring that their rights and well-being are protected in all aspects of the program.

* Work closely with interdisciplinary teams to ensure person-centered care is at the core of all service delivery and interventions.

* Monitor and evaluate participant feedback, addressing any concerns or complaints in a timely and professional manner.

6. Leadership and Strategic Planning:

* Serve as a key member of the senior leadership team, contributing to the strategic direction of the PACE program.

* Collaborate with leadership to set annual goals for quality and compliance performance and develop strategies to achieve these objectives.

* Ensure alignment of quality and compliance initiatives with organizational goals and values.

7. Data Collection and Analysis:

* Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of quality and compliance data to track program performance and outcomes.

* Utilize data to drive decision-making and identify areas for operational improvements and resource allocation.

* Prepare reports and presentations for senior leadership and external stakeholders regarding compliance, quality, and performance metrics.

8. Technology and EMR

* Serving as the primary point of contact for EMR-related issues, providing guidance and troubleshooting support to team members.

* Leading training sessions and providing ongoing support for staff to ensure efficient use of the EMR system.

* Collaborating with IT and management teams to implement updates and resolve system issues.

* Continuously staying updated on new features and best practices for the EMR system to ensure the organization is utilizing the platform to its full potential.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, nursing, public health, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

* Minimum of 4 years of experience in quality management, compliance, or regulatory affairs in a healthcare setting, with at least 2 years in a leadership role.

* Knowledge and experience with PACE program operations and regulations (CMS and state-level).

* Strong understanding of healthcare regulations, accreditation standards, and compliance protocols.

* Proven track record in leading quality improvement initiatives and risk management programs.

* Exceptional leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.

* Ability to work collaboratively across departments and with interdisciplinary teams.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to drive results.

* Certification in Healthcare Quality (CHCQM, CPHQ) or other relevant certifications preferred.

**Physical Demands:**

* Ability to work in an office environment and attend in-person meetings.

* Occasional travel to program sites or regulatory meetings may be required.

**Work Environment:**

* A collaborative, team-oriented atmosphere within a dynamic, fast-paced healthcare environment.

* Commitment to participant-centered care and service excellence.

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
identity_held_roles.description:
**About Genesis**
=================

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

**The role**
------------

We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.

This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
* Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
* Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
* Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
* Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
* Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
* Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
* Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
* Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
* Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

* You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
* You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
* Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
* You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
* You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
* You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
* 8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
* Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.

**Working conditions**
----------------------

Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.

**Why this role**
-----------------

You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.

**How we work**
---------------

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

* **Limitless ambition.** We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
* **Relentless urgency.** Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
* **Type-2 Fun.** Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
* **Radical transparency.** Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
* **Multiculturalism.** We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
* **Team over ego.** Help others, share context, and win as a team.
* **A joyful journey.** We take pride in the craft.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality Engineering and Automation -Information technology
existing_roles.description:
Overview:

ServiceLink is seeking an experienced Director of Quality Engineering and Automation to lead our quality engineering transformation. This leader will be responsible for defining and executing the enterprise quality strategy, modernizing test automation capabilities, establishing quality governance standards, and driving engineering-wide quality improvements.

This role is not a traditional QA management position focused solely on test execution. The Director will serve as the organization’s quality engineering leader, responsible for building scalable automation capabilities, establishing meaningful quality metrics, and influencing software quality outcomes across Engineering, Product, and Release organizations.

The ideal candidate combines deep quality engineering expertise with strong organizational leadership, executive communication skills, and a proven ability to drive meaningful change in highly matrixed environments. Success in this role requires the ability to influence decisions through data, credibility, partnership, and quality leadership rather than direct organizational authority.

ServiceLink is modernizing the mortgage services industry through AI-accelerated engineering, intelligent automation, and next-generation software delivery practices. We empower the nation’s top lenders and financial institutions with advanced technology, data-driven insights, and high-velocity product development models.

As we continue to scale our technology platforms, we are investing in a modern Quality Engineering organization focused on automation, quality governance, engineering excellence, and continuous delivery. Our goal is to transform quality from a downstream testing activity into an engineering capability embedded throughout the software development lifecycle.

**This is a hybrid role, and will be required to work in-office at our Plano, TX office at least 3 days per week. Candidates must be located within reasonable commuting distance of this office and be willing to work in-office on a regular basis.**

**Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require sponsorship for employment visa status now or in the future.**

A DAY IN THE LIFE

In this role, you will…

* Lead quality engineering transformation
* Own enterprise test automation strategy
* Establish quality governance and risk management policies and procedures
* Drive engineering quality excellence
* Influence cross-functional release and product outcomes
* Establish quality metrics and executive reporting
* Lead and develop the Quality Engineering organization

Success Measures

* Automated coverage of critical business workflows.
* Reduction in manual regression testing effort.
* Improved release predictability and confidence.
* Reduction in escaped production defects.
* Increased adoption of shift-left quality practices.
* Expanded developer ownership of quality.
* Enhanced visibility into quality trends and release readiness risks.
* Increased executive confidence in quality governance and software delivery outcomes.

WHO YOU ARE

You possess …

* 10+ years of progressive experience in software quality, quality engineering, software engineering, or related technology leadership roles.
* 5+ years of experience leading quality engineering organizations in complex enterprise software environments.
* Demonstrated success leading large-scale test automation and quality transformation initiatives.
* Experience building and scaling automation frameworks and engineering quality practices.
* Strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and cloud-native application architectures.
* Experience implementing API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
* Experience establishing quality metrics, executive scorecards, and data-driven governance models.
* Strong understanding of risk management, release readiness, and quality governance practices.
* Experience managing distributed teams and complex organizational change efforts.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and business audiences.
* Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering and testing tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies.

Responsibilities:

1. Lead Quality Engineering Transformation

* Define and execute a multi-year quality engineering strategy aligned with ServiceLink’s technology and business objectives.
* Transform the organization from a predominantly manual testing model to an automation-first quality engineering approach.
* Establish scalable operating models, standards, and best practices across quality engineering functions.
* Evaluate and implement AI-assisted testing capabilities where they provide measurable business value.
* Continuously improve testing effectiveness, release confidence, and overall software quality.
* Develop a strategic roadmap that reduces manual regression testing effort while improving coverage and reliability.

2. Own Enterprise Test Automation Strategy

* Define and execute automation strategies spanning unit, API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing.
* Build and maintain modern automation frameworks supporting multiple product portfolios and technology stacks.
* Identify opportunities to automate repetitive testing activities and reduce release-cycle effort.
* Establish automation standards, coding practices, and framework governance.
* Drive automation adoption across engineering teams and development pipelines.
* Ensure automation investments directly support business outcomes through measurable reductions in manual testing effort

and improved release quality.

3. Establish Quality Governance and Risk Management

* Define enterprise quality standards, testing policies, and release readiness criteria.
* Develop risk-based testing frameworks that focus resources on the highest-value business scenarios.
* Provide objective assessments of release readiness and software quality risks.
* Establish processes for identifying, documenting, communicating, and escalating quality concerns.
* Lead post-release reviews and quality retrospectives to identify systemic improvement opportunities.
* Create clear mechanisms for risk visibility and executive decision support.

4. Drive Engineering Quality Excellence

* Partner with software engineering leaders to embed quality throughout the SDLC.
* Champion shift-left testing practices and developer ownership of quality.
* Promote increased use of automated testing within CI/CD pipelines.
* Drive adoption of engineering practices that improve code quality, testability, maintainability, and system reliability.
* Collaborate with architecture and development teams to improve overall product quality and reduce defect introduction

rates.

* Influence engineering decisions through quality metrics, technical insights, and continuous improvement recommendations.

5. Influence Cross-Functional Release and Product Outcomes

* Build strong working relationships across Product Management, Release Management, Engineering, Operations, and

Support organizations.

* Serve as a trusted advisor on quality, testing strategy, release readiness, and operational risk.
* Influence planning, prioritization, and release decisions through data-driven recommendations and quality insights.
* Ensure stakeholders understand the quality implications of scope changes, late-stage modifications, and release decisions.
* Foster organizational alignment around quality objectives and customer experience outcomes.
* Facilitate constructive discussions regarding risk, readiness, and delivery trade-offs.

6. Establish Quality Metrics and Executive Reporting

* Define and maintain enterprise quality KPIs and executive dashboards.
* Track and communicate trends related to:

o Escaped defects

o Automation coverage

o Regression testing effort

o Test effectiveness

o Production incidents

o Release quality

o Customer-impacting defects

* Use quantitative analysis to identify improvement opportunities and support investment decisions.
* Provide executive leadership with clear visibility into quality trends, risks, and organizational progress.

7. Lead and Develop the Quality Engineering Organization

* Build, mentor, and develop high-performing quality engineering teams.
* Create career paths for automation engineers, quality engineers, and quality leaders.
* Attract and retain top quality engineering talent.
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous learning, and operational excellence.
* Ensure organizational structures support both immediate delivery needs and long-term quality transformation goals.

Qualifications:

Required

* 10+ years of progressive experience in software quality, quality engineering, software engineering, or related technology leadership roles.
* 5+ years of experience leading quality engineering organizations in complex enterprise software environments.
* Demonstrated success leading large-scale test automation and quality transformation initiatives.
* Experience building and scaling automation frameworks and engineering quality practices.
* Strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, CI/CD pipelines, DevOps, and cloud-native application architectures.
* Experience implementing API, integration, end-to-end, performance, and regression testing strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct authority.
* Experience establishing quality metrics, executive scorecards, and data-driven governance models.
* Strong understanding of risk management, release readiness, and quality governance practices.
* Experience managing distributed teams and complex organizational change efforts.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and business audiences.
* Experience leveraging AI-assisted engineering and testing tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or similar technologies.

Preferred

* Experience leading quality engineering organizations undergoing significant automation transformation.
* Background in highly regulated industries such as financial services, mortgage, banking, insurance, healthcare, or fintech.
* Experience implementing quality engineering practices within Agile and product-oriented delivery models.
* Knowledge of modern test automation platforms, quality engineering frameworks, and observability tools.
* Experience supporting large-scale digital transformation initiatives.

existing_roles.description:
**Corporate Overview**

Aluris Sciences is a contract manufacturing organization (CMO) headquartered in Carlsbad, CA with over 50,000 square feet of manufacturing space. The company is dedicated to serving highly innovative companies in the life sciences, diagnostics, drug-device, and combination product industries. Aluris is a full-service, cost-effective partner, providing complete solutions across technical transfer, formulation, filling, lyophilization, assembly, and final kitting of reagents, consumables, and combination products. Aluris provides quality and regulatory expertise to assure the highest in quality manufacturing and supply chain excellence.

**Position Overview**

The Director of Quality Assurance (QA) is responsible for leading and managing the company’s quality assurance and regulatory compliance programs. This role ensures that all quality systems align with regulatory requirements and industry best practices, maintaining compliance with ISO-13485, ISO 14971, GMP/GLP, QSR, 21 CFR 820.30, and other relevant medical device (IVD) regulations.

The Director of QA will work closely with the Vice President of Quality and Regulatory to develop and implement strategic quality initiatives, oversee external audits and regulatory inspections, and drive continuous improvement across the organization. This role also involves coaching and mentoring staff, managing compliance metrics, and supporting client engagements by serving as the company’s quality systems representative.

Success in this position requires strong leadership, a deep understanding of quality regulations, excellent communication skills, and the ability to build and maintain a culture of compliance and operational excellence.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and assist in performing all tasks necessary to achieve the organization's mission and help execute growth
* Work with the Vice President of Quality and Regulatory to formulation and execute the
* strategic vision.
* Work with the Vice President of Quality and Regulatory to develop and actively manage the company's quality system consistent with the culture and intent of the company
* Oversee and coordinate the quality management systems implementation.
* Accountable for maintaining a state of compliance to f CFR 21 820, 210 and 211.
* Act as the "management representative" within the quality plan.
* Will formulate and lead the management team to maintain ISO 13485 compliance.
* Will assist the leadership in implementation of the technology and process capability roadmap with specific emphasis on validation (10/OQ) and documentation support.
* Will be involved in strategic planning, evaluation, and professional development initiatives.
* Will recruit, hire and manage a motivated and highly talented staff of quality and regulatory professionals
* Provide leadership and/or support as needed throughout the organization, specifically all activities associated with bill of materials structuring, part numbering, SKU attributes, set up, training and quality management systems.
* Represent the quality systems acumen and quality systems capabilities of the company.
* Support all clients engagements as the quality system voice of the company and our capabilities
* Will actively work with the VP of Manufacturing to solve challenges in the production environment related to workflow, internal audits, material dispositions (MRP) and process changes/deviations.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Successfully served in a similar capacity in a contract manufacturing company for a highly regulated market, preferably the life science/pharmaceutical environment.
* Proven credibility as a Quality leader in the life science manufacturing environment.
* Experience and familiarity in reagent formulation, filling and finishing activities with several years of directly related accountability for quality in this form of manufacturing.
* Proven track record of exceptional performance in these FDA regulated environments with audit experience from the FDA and clients
* FDA rapport and relationships are strongly desired
* A familiarity with Lean Manufacturing cultures in a volume production facility
* Experience and proven results in driving process/technology validation efforts.
* Experience and expertise in communication exchanges with clients during tours, meetings, and audits.
* Consistently exhibited through their actions, decisions, and interactions (internally and externally), the highest standards of ethics and integrity.
* The ability to create, direct and implement corporate objectives in an environment with a high sense of urgency
* A proven capability to generate shareholder value
* Negotiation skills to maximize value in client/regulatory body discussions
* Experience building compliance and standardization of processes (building a scalable organization).
* Experience participating in ERP implementations managing and driving documentation control, bills of materials, routings and workflows.
* A track record of recruiting exceptional talent within the economic constraints of a small company.
* A "hands-on" management style with the interpersonal skills required to build a successful team and the desire to motivate, inspire and develop management team members
* High intelligence with effective analytical and problem-solving skills.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills and listening skills.
* A proactive style using initiative and perseverance in order to bring about meaningful change.
* Demonstrated high energy.
* Team Player.

**What to Expect:**

This is a full-time, 100% on-site position based in Carlsbad, CA, with a Monday–Friday schedule and 8-hour workdays, excluding meal breaks. Overtime, weekend, and holiday work may be required as business needs arise.

The position offers a flexible start time between 6:00 a.m. and 9:30 a.m.; however, employees are expected to maintain a consistent schedule. Any exceptions to the established schedule must be approved in advance by the manager.

**What We Offer/Compensation**

At Aluris Sciences, LLC. we value our employees and are proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and financial future. Eligible employees enjoy:

**Health & Wellness**

* Medical, dental and vision coverage
* Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options
* Company-paid life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage

**Financial & Time Off**

* 401(k) plan with company match
* Paid vacation
* California Paid Sick Leave
* Paid company holidays

**Additional Benefits**

* Employee Assistance Program
* Voluntary and supplemental benefit options

The pay range for this position is $195,000 - $205,000 annually. The final compensation offered will be based on a variety of job-related factors, including geographic location, skills, education, experience, certifications, and other relevant qualifications.

**Organization Overview:**

Sound Community Services, Inc. (SCSI) is a private, not-for-profit organization dedicated to educating, assisting, and supporting individuals with persistent mental illness and substance use disorders. We work tirelessly to create a culture and environment in which recovery and wellness are possible.

**Position Overview:**

The Director of Quality Assurance (QA) oversees all agency activities related to quality improvement, compliance, data integrity, and regulatory preparedness for the agency. This position provides leadership in the development, implementation, and monitoring of systems that support clinical excellence, consumer rights, performance measurement, and regulatory compliance. The Director plays a critical role in the maintenance, configuration, and optimization of the Electronic Health Record (EHR); oversees required state reporting; maintains the centralized repository of all Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) reported data; and ensures accurate and timely data submission. This role also leads the agency’s preparation for external audits (ex., Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF), Department of Public Health (DPH), DMHAS), coordinates customer satisfaction activities, and serves as the agency’s Client Rights Officer.

This position is responsible for the monitoring and analyzing of processes to meet Fidelity and contractual requirements across the agency. Ongoing analysis of health care information obtained from a variety of sources, including patient care, financial, and demographic data is necessary. This role involves the development and preparation of information for state reporting and organizational best practices. This position will maintain repository of all state reported data for all DMHAS programs. A heavy importance is placed on collaborating with program leaders across the agency, ensuring accuracy of data reported and driving agency performance.

**Essential Functions**

**Department Leadership, Training, and Support**

* Directly supervise two (2) employees in the Quality Assurance department and serve as backup to staff as needed.
* Provide Daily Living Activities Functional Assessment (DLA-20), program specific documentation, and recovery planning training to the agency.
* Train employees and monitor compliance across programs with state reporting requirements.
* Function as an internal information expert to the entire management team when special and critical quality issues occur.
* Consult with senior leadership to resolve quality, service, and efficiency problems.

**State Reporting, Data, and Surveys**

* Facilitate and coordinate annual DMHAS Consumer Satisfaction Surveys and quarterly CARF Satisfaction surveys.
* Provide DMHAS Data Performance System (DDaP) data and informational support to other departments, including DDaP 101 supervisor training, share DMHAS information with leadership, and present quarterly and annual DMHAS Report Cards to leadership.

**Electronic Health Record (EHR) and Systems Support**

* Triage QA tickets. Issues include, but are not limited to, document management, on/off-boarding, medical staff onboarding, system outages, etc.
* Facilitate within the EHR the build and support of procedures, forms, and form development; implement training to identified employees.
* Foster ongoing support to assigned programs and serve as a liaison between staff and vendors for effective responses to users’ needs.

**Audit Readiness, Compliance, and Quality Improvement**

* Provide support to programs in preparation for routine external audits, including CARF survey, fidelity reviews, and Department of Public Health licensing.
* Facilitate completion of all corrective action plans and audit follow-up, including quarterly and annual program compliance reviews.
* Monitor and assist with corrections and work with programs to identify and resolve root causes as needed.
* Ensure compliance with SCSI’s policies, quality assurance programs, and safety; ensure EHR compliance with regulatory agencies like DMHAS, DPH, CARF, etc.
* Participate in quality improvement initiatives.
* Serve as the agency’s Client Rights Officer (CRO), observing and adhering to the role outlined by DMHAS.

**Agency Participation and Policy Compliance**

* Participate in all agency activities pertaining to health and safety, training, drills, etc.
* Adhere to SCSI policies and procedures.

**Physical Requirements**

The employee frequently is required to walk, talk and/or hear; speaking and hearing ability sufficient to communicate effectively by phone or in person at normal volumes; vision adequate to read correspondence, computer screen, forms, etc. The employee is occasionally required to stand and climb or balance. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly.
* Demonstrated technology and software application skills; ability to learn new software packages; highly skilled in office productivity software (e.g., Word, PowerPoint, Excel, email).
* Excellent written and oral communication skills.
* Ability to be proactive, flexible, and customer service focused and to work effectively with others.

**Qualifications**

**Minimum education:** Bachelor’s degree required, or an equivalent combination of education and related experience.

**Minimum experience:** Experience working with electronic health record system, i.e., CareLogic; experience providing training; and experience with accreditation standards such as CARF, DMHAS, DPH, or similar regulatory bodies.

The role is accountable for safe, compliant, inspection-ready, and predictable execution across a seven-day operating model, including product release and in-process testing, STAT support to Manufacturing, environmental and microbiological testing, raw material disposition, stability support, sample management, and analytical lifecycle enablement. The Senior Director establishes the QC operating strategy, capacity and resource plan, performance system, and leadership model required to meet manufacturing, client, and business commitments while sustaining laboratory excellence and data integrity.

**Here's What You'll Do**

**QC Strategy and Leadership**

* Lead the integrated QC organization, operating model, objectives, decision rights, talent strategy, and capability roadmap.
* Develop QC management and technical leaders while aligning headcount, seven-day coverage, facilities, equipment, systems, operating expense, and capital with demand.

**Predictable QC Operations and Laboratory Excellence**

existing_roles.description:
**Company Overview:**

ChocXO Chocolatier LLC is a leading North American premium chocolate manufacturer grounded in innovation, quality, and sustainability. We are a fast-growing, vertically integrated food manufacturing company operating across branded CPG and contract manufacturing. In the past year, we have scaled from one manufacturing facility to two, expanded our brand portfolio, and invested heavily in new capacity, innovation, and infrastructure.

**Our footprint includes Delta, British Columbia:**

Our 60,000 sq ft, fully automated, SQF Level 3 operational flagship, and Rockwall, Texas: Our new 225,000 sq ft manufacturing and warehouse complex, scheduled to open in 2027. We are now at the stage where systems, discipline, and repeatability matter as much as growth. We are building an enterprise-grade operations platform designed to scale—not a collection of plants dependent on heroics. We foster a culture of accountability where professionals thrive in structured environments and uphold rigorous standards.

**The Role:**  
The VP, Manufacturing & Operations reports directly to the President and leads plant operations at both of ChocXO’s manufacturing facilities: Delta, British Columbia and Rockwall, Texas. The Plant Managers at each location report directly to this role. The VP is the senior leader accountable for end-to-end operational performance across both sites, including manufacturing execution, food safety leadership, QA capability, OT systems oversight, and operational excellence.  
This is a hands-on, high-accountability leadership role. It requires deep manufacturing judgment, disciplined execution, and the confidence to stop production, reset standards, and enforce compliance when required.  
Key Responsibilities  
Multi-Plant Leadership

* Directly lead, develop, and hold accountable the Plant Managers for Delta, BC and Rockwall, TX
* Establish consistent expectations, KPIs, and operating cadence across all sites
* Ensure alignment between plant-level execution and enterprise standards
* Be visibly present in plants — especially during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions

Operational Technology (OT) & Systems

* Provide leadership and oversight for OT systems supporting manufacturing operations
* Production monitoring
* Process controls
* Data integrity
* System discipline
* Ensure OT systems support repeatability, visibility, and accountability, not workarounds
* Partner with engineering and IT, but own operational effectiveness of systems on the floor

Food Safety, Quality & Audit Readiness

* Provide senior leadership on food safety expectations and audit readiness
* Set the standard for:
* Regulatory compliance
* Customer audits
* Third-party food safety certifications
* Build and lead a strong, credible QA organization
* Ensure quality systems are proactive, documented, and enforced — not reactive or cosmetic
* Personally set the tone that food safety and quality are non-negotiable

Process Discipline & Validation

* Establish and enforce standardized operating procedures (SOPs)
* Own process validation, trial approval, and GO / NO-GO decision gates
* Eliminate reliance on undocumented adjustments, heroics, or tribal knowledge
* Ensure processes run within defined parameters, with normal staffing, on repeat days

Inventory, Scrap & Loss Control

* Own accountability for scrap, rework, obsolete inventory, and yield loss
* Implement root-cause analysis and corrective action discipline
* Drive early-warning indicators and corrective action — not post-event explanations
* Embed cost awareness without compromising safety or quality

Training, Safety & Accountability Culture

* Build structured training systems for operators, supervisors, and plant leadership
* Lead facility safety as a core operational priority
* Establish and enforce an accountability culture:
* Clear expectations
* clear consequences
* Consistent follow-through
* Partner with HR, but retain operational authority and standards

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

* Drive operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and morale
* Standardize best practices across plants
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives grounded in data and discipline
* Ensure improvements are institutionalized, not personality-dependent

AI, Automation & Digital Efficiency

* Use AI and advanced analytics to drive efficiency, throughput, and yield improvement across manufacturing and warehouse operations
* Identify, evaluate, and deploy practical AI tools (e.g., predictive maintenance, demand and production scheduling, quality and vision inspection, downtime and scrap analysis)
* Leverage AI-enabled insights from OT and ERP data to make faster, fact-based decisions and catch issues before they become losses
* Build team capability and comfort with AI tools, ensuring adoption is disciplined, documented, and compliant with food safety and data integrity requirements

What Success Looks Like

* Plant Managers are strong, accountable leaders — not firefighters
* Food safety audits are predictable, calm, and well-prepared
* QA is respected, not overridden
* OT systems provide clarity and control, not noise
* Scrap, rework, and operational “surprises” trend down materially
* Operations run consistently across plants and shifts
* The President is not required to intervene in day-to-day operations
* AI and automation tools are delivering measurable gains in efficiency, yield, and uptime

Required Experience & Profile  
Experience

* 15+ years in food manufacturing operations
* Proven multi-plant leadership experience
* Deep, practical expertise in:
* Food safety systems
* Quality assurance
* Audit management
* Allergen control
* Sanitation validation
* Process control
* Experience scaling operations in fast-growth environments
* Sufficient, hands-on experience applying AI, automation, and data analytics in a manufacturing environment to drive measurable efficiency gains
* Cross-border operations experience (U.S./Canada) strongly preferred

Leadership Attributes

* Exceptionally detail-oriented
* Disciplined, methodical, and structured
* Calm, firm, and decisive
* Comfortable holding leaders accountable
* Respected on the plant floor — not theatrical, not passive
* Strong presence without ego
* Comfortable saying “no” to bad ideas, shortcuts, or pressure

What We Are Not Looking For

* “Idea-first” operators without execution depth
* Leaders who normalize exceptions and workarounds
* Consultants masquerading as operators
* People who rely on heroics instead of systems
* Anyone uncomfortable enforcing standards or stopping production

Location & Travel

* Based at Rockwall, TX (DFW area). This is a fully on-site role, not remote, because presence matters
* Regular travel between the Rockwall and Delta plants is required, including during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions
* Must be able to travel between the U.S. and Canada

Why This Role Matters  
This role is central to building a durable, scalable manufacturing platform.

**The right leader will:**

* Bring order to complexity
* Reduce operational risk
* Strengthen food safety and quality credibility
* Enable profitable, disciplined growth

If you are a serious food manufacturing operations leader who believes strong systems beat heroics, we want to talk.

existing_roles.description:
**Supply Chain and Production Director**

**Purpose**

The Supply Chain and Production Director is the owner of the operating system for our steel fabrication and assembly business, with accountability for manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics, and operational strategy. Reporting directly to the Vice President, General Manager, and operating within a collaborative French corporate structure this leader translates business strategy and commercial demand into integrated capacity, investment, sourcing, inventory, and execution priorities while remaining closely connected to shop-floor performance.  
The immediate mandate is to lead a multi-year factory modernization and growth initiative. Working with an experienced production and sourcing team, this role will execute capital deployments—including robotic welding cells, laser cutting, CNC machining, and other processes—to improve throughput, labor productivity, margins, and the factory’s overall cost profile. In parallel, the Director will partner with Product Marketing and Engineering to optimize a complex, +2,000-SKU finished goods inventory footprint, improve working-capital efficiency, and deliver required service levels.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Factory Modernization & Automation (Immediate Priority)**

* **Automation Roadmap:** Lead the industrial design and execution of the automation master plan to reduce structural labor costs, improve margins, and increase production throughput.
* **CapEx Management:** Own the execution of the lifecycle from vendor selection through commissioning.
* **Systems Integration:** Partner with engineering and IT to integrate the machinery with the necessary digital layers, moving toward a more data driven environment, and having the necessary people trained for new technology (i.e, programming and jig building).

**2. Production Planning & SKU Management**

* **High-Mix Scheduling:** Optimize production scheduling and OTIF for a complex 2,000-SKU environment, balancing inventory, utilization and efficiency.
* **WIP Optimization:** Establish strict controls for Work-in-Process (WIP) material to eliminate structural bottlenecks between initial fabrication and down-stream welding/painting/assembly operations.
* **MPS & S&OP Ownership:** Oversee a quarterly Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) process and drive the MPS to closely align plant capacity with commercial demand.

**3. End-to-End Supply Chain & Procurement**

* **Material Sourcing Strategy:** Manage raw steel and components procurement, navigating volatility through proactive vendor management and diversification.
* **Inventory Control:** Implement strict inventory analysis, flow management and cycle-counting programs to maximize inventory turnover while ensuring high service levels.
* **Logistics & Warehousing:** Oversee inbound material flow and outbound freight logistics to minimize total cost-to-serve.

**4. Leadership & Culture Transformation**

* **Change Management:** Champion the shift from legacy manual labor workflows to an automated, technically skilled operating environment, actively retraining and upskilling the existing workforce.
* **Scope:** Lead Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, and Production Supervisors while collaborating with Site Leadership, Safety, Maintenance, and Shipping leaders.
* **Safety & Compliance:** Establish and reinforce a world-class safety culture by partnering with site leaders to integrate safety expectations, regulatory compliance, risk reduction, and corrective-action discipline into daily operations and capital-project execution.

**Qualifications**

**Minimum Qualifications**

* **Experience:** 10–15+ years of progressive operational leadership experience within an industrial manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a site leadership role (e.g., Plant Manager, Director of Operations).
* **Industry Sector:** Deep, proven track record in structural steel, sheet metal fabrication, machining, or heavy industrial equipment environment.
* **Automation Track Record:** Direct, verifiable experience successfully implementing robotics or automated cells on a manufacturing floor.
* **Scale Comfort:** Prior experience operating within and/or scaling a $25M–$100M revenue business; highly comfortable with mid-market resource boundaries and high-growth demands.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or Operations.

**Technical & System Skills**

* Deep knowledge of metal fabrication processes.
* Lean Manufacturing / Six Sigma and Kaizen expertise.
* Strong financial acumen with detailed experience managing localized operational budgets.
* Advanced experience with mid-market ERP systems—Epicor.

Located close to the Michigan/Ohio border, Toledo Tool and Die has diligently served the people of both of those great states since 1940. Today Toledo Tool & Die has four facilities in the Toledo area and one in Pioneer, Ohio.

Toledo Tool & Die is looking for a **Plant Manager** to join our team to support our continued growth.

This is a full-time position based in Toledo, Ohio. We offer competitive wages, growth opportunities, and a clean, safe work environment.

**WHAT TOLEDO TOOL & DIE CAN OFFER YOU:**

* 401k

* Previous experience at the plant manager level or equivalent

* Positive attitude

* Willingness to learn
* Safety minded

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, direction, and operational performance of an automotive manufacturing facility. This role ensures the plant meets or exceeds expectations for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee engagement while driving continuous improvement and operational excellence. The Plant Manager provides strategic leadership to all plant functions—including Production, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Materials, HR, and EHS—ensuring alignment with organizational goals and customer requirements. Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

### **ABOUT THE JOB**

The Vice President, Manufacturing Engineering holds executive accountability for defining, scaling, and optimizing all aspects of manufacturing engineering across the entire Anduril enterprise. This role encompasses strategic development, execution of multi-year operational roadmaps, technological and process advancement, and organizational leadership across all product lines, production sites, and divisions. The VP will ensure consistent, rapid, and high-standard execution, driving efficiency, scale, and performance that directly contribute to Anduril's mission and market leadership. This role sits centrally and is responsible for ensuring that every division builds against a common standard.

### **WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Own the overarching manufacturing engineering strategy, operational roadmap, and resource budget for Anduril's centralized manufacturing engineering organization.
* Develop and champion a multi-year scaling strategy to meet exponential growth targets, changing operational constraints, and evolving customer demands.
* Strategically allocate resources (talent, capital, systems, facilities) across competing priorities, balancing urgent tactical needs with long-term capability building.
* Establish and enforce the enterprise standard for how Anduril builds production line operation, manufacturing systems usage, process design, and engineering practice, and hold division production leadership accountable to it.
* Own the roadmap for centralized capabilities, ensuring they are built to scale across product lines.
* Partner with and influence the VPs and Heads of Production across all divisions, setting technical direction for organizations that do not report to you.
* Drive consistency in how manufacturing engineering roles are defined, leveled, and expected to perform at every Anduril site, and deploy leadership and IC talent across the enterprise accordingly.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* 15+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering, production operations, or industrial engineering within a hardware/physical-product environment, with 5–7+ years at the executive level (VP or Senior Director) leading multi-team or multi-site organizations.
* Exceptional presentation, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills; capable of aligning C-suite leaders and motivating frontline operators alike.
* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Aerospace Engineering (or a related engineering/technical discipline). Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* Eligible to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.

#### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience navigating high-mix/low-volume transitions into high-volume/mass delivery.
* Background in fast-paced, high-accountability sectors (e.g., aerospace, defense, deep-tech, autonomous systems, high-growth industrial tech).

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. ### **Data Privacy**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering is responsible for leading manufacturing quality across two Entegris manufacturing sites in Texas and translating global quality standards and quality priorities into consistent site execution. This role provides multi-site leadership to reduce risk, strengthen process capability, improve customer satisfaction, and deliver measurable quality improvements across the two-site footprint.  
  
The Senior Manager partners with site Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Customer Quality, Product Quality and Quality Systems teams to embed quality ownership into daily operations. This leader is accountable for site quality performance, consistent implementation of quality standards, compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements, and the development of capable site quality teams. The role leads through site quality leaders and teams, establishes clear ownership and follow-through, and escalates risks and resource needs to North America quality leadership.

The hired individual will work on-site at our Burnet, TX location with some travel to our Decatur, TX location.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Lead manufacturing quality across all two sites through site quality leaders and teams; clarify responsibilities, prioritize resources based on risk, and maintain regular on-site engagement.
* Ensure consistent implementation of global quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices; maintain audit readiness and timely closure of findings at each site.
* Partner with site Operations leaders to establish quality roadmaps, objectives, and common key performance indicators (KPIs); conduct routine cross-site reviews and drive recovery plans where performance falls short.

Apnimed is a rapidly growing pharmaceutical company working to transform the treatment of sleep apnea based on a simple idea – patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) could benefit from treatment with a safe and effective oral medication dosed once daily at bedtime. Our lead development program, AD109, targets the neurologic control of upper airway muscles to maintain an open airway during sleep. Apnimed is committed to innovation, as well as state-of-the-art advancements in sleep medicine, which is leading to the development of a portfolio of novel pharmacologic therapies for sleep apnea and related disorders.

Recognized by the Boston Business Journal as one of the Best Places to Work in both 2024 and 2025, we are continuing to grow and build the foundational operations that enable our employees and our mission to thrive.

The Senior Manager, Quality Systems & Compliance reports to the Senior Director, GCP Quality Assurance and Quality Compliance and is responsible for administering, maintaining, and continuously improving Apnimed's electronic Quality Management System (eQMS) and associated quality processes, and for keeping them inspection-ready. The successful candidate will also play a key role in strengthening the Quality Management System infrastructure as a business partner across GxP and corporate quality functions, ensuring quality processes remain compliant, scalable, and aligned with the company's transition toward commercialization. This is an exciting opportunity to strengthen the quality infrastructure that supports Apnimed as part of a major paradigm shift in the treatment of sleep apnea from medical devices and surgery to a first in class pharmaceutical treatment.

* Serve as subject matter expert and administrator for the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), evaluating proposed system changes and coordinating testing, validation, and deployment activities.

* Maintain system documentation, including procedures, work instructions, validation documentation, and configuration records.

**Requirements**

* Demonstrated experience managing electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS), including administering or supporting platforms such as Dot Compliance, Veeva Quality, MasterControl, TrackWise Digital, ComplianceWire, or similar.
* Working knowledge of FDA, EMA, ICH, GCP, GMP, and GLP requirements.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and external/internal audits.
* Preferred: Direct administrator experience with Veeva Quality, and experience with computerized system validation (CSV) and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.

existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE JOB**  
  
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering and systems to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production in Waltham, MA. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Your leadership will also guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing's capacity commitments while driving advancements in digital tools and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable approach to solving complex manufacturing challenges in a highly dynamic environment.  
  
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team:** Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers and technical staff. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* **Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology:** Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril Imaging's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
* **Lead New Product Introduction (NPI):** Partner with R&D and product development teams to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM) and Design for Assembly (DfA) principles early in the development cycle to de-risk production scaling.
* **Scale Production Capability:** Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
* **Drive Continuous Improvement & Complexity Reduction:** Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive commonality optimization, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization to simplify production at scale.
* **Resource & Budget Management:** Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electro-mechanical or imaging hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
* Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
* Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
* Familiarity with optical system integration and test, precision assembly, or imaging hardware manufacturing.
* Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
* Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and PLM, MES, and ERP systems.
* Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
* Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. existing_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.

existing_roles.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is hiring a Director of Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Quality to build and lead the team responsible for the technical relationship with our supplier base, from first sketch through high-volume production, and for the quality systems that ensure everything that arrives at our factories meets spec. This role reports into our VP, Global Supply Chain and brings together two functions that have to move as one: the engineers who industrialize our components and equipment, and the quality systems and team that hold our suppliers accountable once they are producing.

Form's 85% domestically sourced supply chain was built for a battery chemistry with no existing supplier base, which means the industrialization playbook and the quality systems we need are still being written. You will set that standard: rigorous enough to protect a product with a 100-hour duration promise, and practical enough to work with suppliers who are learning our process alongside us. You will fly high enough to set the strategy and the org, and go deep enough to sit in a root cause review when it matters.  
  
*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Lead Form's Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Supplier Quality organization, growing a team of engineers embedded across battery materials, components, and equipment categories.
* Own the end-to-end industrialization journey for direct materials and made-to-spec components, from design-for-manufacturability review and supplier selection through tooling qualification and sustaining production support.
* Build and own Form's supplier quality management system, including PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and SCAR/8D corrective action processes, calibrated for a novel battery chemistry with no legacy supply base to borrow from.
* Set the technical bar for supplier selection and qualification, partnering with Global Supply Managers to ensure our sourcing strategy is backed by suppliers who can deliver on cost, quality, and schedule.
* Own supplier process capability and yield performance, coordinating with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, and Reliability teams to drive root cause analysis and corrective action when issues surface.
* Develop the roadmap and staffing plan for quality systems aligned to relevant standards (e.g., ISO 9001, IATF 16949) at a scale and stage appropriate to where Form is today and where we are headed.
* Represent supplier technical and quality readiness within the Product Development Process, ensuring every component and supplier is qualified ahead of commercial scale.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to align supplier roadmaps with Form's build plan and deployment targets.

### **What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 12+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, quality, or manufacturing engineering, including at least 5 years in a people leadership role building and scaling a team.
* Demonstrated expertise across DFM/DFA, PPAP, APQP, FMEA, SPC, and structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5 Whys).
* Experience building quality and industrialization systems from the ground up, ideally in a hardware, energy, or battery environment without an established supplier base to lean on.
* Strong technical fluency to go deep with engineers and suppliers, paired with the executive presence to represent risk, tradeoffs, and strategy to senior leadership.
* Comfort operating across the full arc from early design concept through high-volume production and sustaining support, with the judgment to know which problems need a system and which need a phone call.

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*  
  
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*
