existing_roles.title: Plant Manager III
existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

  

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

* Build strong, credible, long-term relationships with customers and ensure plant execution consistently supports quality, delivery, responsiveness, and customer commitments.
* Build strategic relationships with suppliers, equipment manufacturers, contractors, and other external partners critical to the construction, start-up, and ongoing operation of the plant.
* Work collaboratively with customers and suppliers to resolve issues quickly while protecting long-term business relationships.
* Serve as a senior representative of the Greenville operation with business leadership, customers, suppliers, community stakeholders, and other external partners as appropriate.
* Build strong cross-functional relationships across the broader organization and effectively navigate a complex, matrixed environment.
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the plant and foster an employee environment built on communication, engagement, trust, accountability, and strong employee relations.

**Safety, Quality & Culture**

* Establish safety as a foundational operating principle and ensure appropriate systems, behaviors, and leadership accountability are embedded throughout the facility.
* Champion a quality-first mindset and ensure the organization consistently meets internal requirements and customer expectations.
* Build a high-performance culture characterized by accountability, collaboration, transparency, urgency, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear expectations for leadership behavior and ensure those expectations cascade throughout the plant organization.
* Create an environment where employees understand how their work contributes to plant performance, customer success, and the broader business.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
* Significant progressive leadership experience within complex, high-volume, highly automated, or advanced manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading a significant manufacturing operation with accountability across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading the build and start-up of a new manufacturing facility, significant plant expansion, major manufacturing transformation, or complex production ramp-up.
* Strong knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing or relevant advanced manufacturing technologies and processes.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations and the interdependencies among production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people.
* Strong financial and commercial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, capital investments, productivity, and business performance.
* Demonstrated success building, leading, coaching, and developing high-performing leadership teams.
* Experience with workforce planning, organizational design, talent development, and leadership succession.
* Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, executive leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Direct experience in lithium-ion cell manufacturing or large-scale battery manufacturing.
* Experience taking a newly constructed manufacturing facility through commissioning, production launch, volume ramp-up, and stabilized operations.
* Experience with highly automated manufacturing equipment and advanced manufacturing technologies.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, structured problem solving, operational excellence, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization or complex matrixed business environment.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position requires working in a plant/warehouse environment. Therefore, expect varying working conditions.

protected_roles.title: Corporate Food Safety Quality Assurance Director
protected_roles.description:
**We are willing to relocate to Rhode Island area for the right candidate**

We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Corporate Food Safety Quality Assurance Director to lead our food safety and quality assurance programs. The Director will be responsible for ensuring the highest standards of food safety and quality across all operations, developing and implementing policies, and managing compliance with regulatory requirements. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in food safety and quality assurance, with excellent leadership and analytical skills.

### **Duties/Responsibilities:**

* Develop and implement comprehensive food safety programs to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards.

* Oversee quality assurance processes, including product testing, inspections, and audits to maintain high-quality standards.

* Create and enforce food safety and quality policies and procedures across all operations.

* Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal food safety regulations, including FDA, USDA, and HACCP standards.

* Identify and manage food safety risks, implementing corrective actions and preventive measures.

* Develop and deliver training programs to educate employees on food safety and quality assurance practices.

* Monitor and analyze food safety and quality metrics to identify areas for improvement and implement the best practices.

* Lead and mentor the food safety and quality assurance team, fostering a collaborative and high-performance work environment.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders, including suppliers, customers, and regulatory agencies.

### **Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Exceptional leadership skills with the ability to inspire and motivate a diverse team.

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively convey complex food safety information.

* Strong attention to detail and accuracy in food safety and quality assurance processes.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make data-driven decisions.

* Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

* Proficiency with food safety and quality assurance software, systems, and Microsoft Office Suite.

### **Education and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in food science, Microbiology, or a related field is required.

* Master's degree or relevant certification (e.g., HACCP, SQF, PCQI) is highly preferred.

* A minimum of 10 years of experience in food safety and quality assurance roles, with a proven track record of success.

* Extensive experience with food safety regulations, standards, and compliance.
* Proven ability to lead and develop high-performing teams.

### **Working Conditions:**

* Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends as needed.

* Availability for occasional travel to meet with stakeholders and attend industry events.

* Ability to thrive in a high-pressure environment and make critical food safety decisions under stress.

* Flexibility to work remotely, when necessary, while maintaining effective communication and oversight.

* Willingness to work extended hours during peak business periods or crises.

* Managing food safety and quality assurance operations across multiple time zones and cultures, requiring adaptability and cultural sensitivity.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

protected_roles.description:
**Your Opportunity as the Senior Manager Quality Assurance - Uncrustables**

This role is critical to ensure our Frozen Handheld & Spreads plants consistently meet our high standards for food safety and quality, as well as regulatory and customer requirements. You will lead quality assurance efforts across three sandwich manufacturing facilities and R&D pilot plant, balancing strategic oversight with hands-on project execution. Success in this role requires adaptability, attention to detail, and the ability to lead through influence.

**Location:** Orrville. OH Corporate

**Work Arrangements:**

* Hybrid – onsite a minimum of 9 days a month, primarily during core weeks as determined by the Company; maybe more as business need requires

* Flexibility to work outside of core hours, flow to the work, and travel to support plant / bakery issues as needed

* Travel – up to 35% annually

* Typically requires working 45+ hours per week, including on call

**In this role you will:**

* Provide leadership through being the primary liaison between Corporate QA and Uncrustables manufacturing facilities

* Assure the manufacturing facilities are in compliance with JMS Quality and Food safety policies and procedures; all Federal, State and local regulatory requirements including Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) and Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) and any other applicable certifications.

* Drive and support each facility’s Operational Excellence (OpsEx) journey with quality loss elimination tasks by supporting the use of Quality Pillar tools and the integration within other OpsEx Pillars.

* Responsible for the development and mentorship of the plant JMS QA managers and their teams as well as one salaried direct report.

* Conduct/Lead 19 Key Element operational QA audits with JMS CQA team and follow up with plant teams on identified gaps and corrective/preventative actions (CAPA).

* Lead/participate as CQA representative in improvement projects with Uncrustables plant teams and our cross functional partners (R&D, TSO, Engineering, etc.)

* Drive continual quality improvement as measured by Quality key performance indicators including internal and external audits, and company quality metrics

* Provide technical support to the manufacturing plants and R&D as it relates to, but not limited to, quality and food safety requirements.

* Assist in the management of plant quality non-conformances and escalations with the goal of investigating root cause and implementing corrective/preventative actions to prevent incident reoccurrence.

* Collaborate with Plant Managers, Ops VP/Directors to build predictive quality into the manufacturing process.

* Participate on the corporate crisis team, as needed.

**What we are looking for:**

Minimum Requirements:

* A bachelor's degree

* 7 years of progressive quality and food safety experience

* 2 years of experience in manufacturing setting

* Experience working with at least 2 distinct product types

* Demonstrated people management experience (small to mid-size teams) and the ability to lead and work in a cross-functional and team-oriented environment

* Strong knowledge of quality assurance, food manufacturing, packaging, processing and distribution; USDA HACCP, FDA FSMA, GFSI (BRCGS)

Additional skills and experience that we think would make someone successful in this role:

* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Biology, Microbiology or related scientific degree

* Previous experience in low-moisture ready-to-eat (RTE) foods (strongly preferred)

* Previous experience in bread manufacturing with focus in bread quality

* Strong quantitative and qualitative assessment skills, critical thinking skills and the ability to constructively challenge ideas and assumptions

* Proven capabilities in project management with ability to lead multiple and concurrent projects

* Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (human food) or HACCP experience

* Takes initiative, manages time effectively, and is motivated to achieve goals without constant oversight. You’re proactive in identifying opportunities and solving problems independently.

* Thrives in a dynamic environment and is comfortable navigating change. Whether it's shifting priorities or new technologies, you remain flexible and focused.

* Demonstrated high level of organizational skills and ability

* Proven ability to develop written tools, Policies, SOPs.

* Demonstrated ability with continuous improvement

* Demonstrated ability to work in cross-functional & team-oriented environment with multiple disciplines while providing leadership through influence rather than authority

**The Right Place for You**

We are bold, kind, strive to do the right thing, we play to win, and we believe in a strong community that thrives together. Our culture is rooted in our Basic Beliefs , and we believe in supporting every employee by meeting their physical, emotional, and financial needs.

We're an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, age, national origin, disability status or protected veteran status.

protected_roles.title: VP, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Dexter Magnetic Technologies supplies specialized magnetic solutions and components to demanding applications in the medical, aerospace, defense, semiconductor manufacturing, oil and gas, and industrial end markets. Dexter’s engineers solve complex customer problems with innovative solutions, winning business based on quality, customer support, and application engineering expertise.

For more information on Dexter Magnetic Technologies, please visit: https://www.dextermag.com/ (https://www.dextermag.com/).

**Job Summary**

The Division VP of Quality is the senior Quality executive for the Division and is responsible for establishing and executing the Division’s Quality strategy, systems, standards, and culture.

  

This position provides strategic leadership to ensure the Division consistently delivers safe, reliable, compliant, and high-quality products and services that meet or exceed customer expectations while supporting the company’s growth, profitability, and operational objectives.

  

The role partners closely with Division leaders across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Commercial, Finance, and Human Resources to establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, prevention, and customer excellence.

  

This position also serves as the subject matter expert for the enterprise-wide Permag Quality Management System and related regulatory and certification requirements, including ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, ITAR, and other applicable customer, industry, and regulatory requirements. In this capacity this position supports and coordinates quality systems activities at sites across the entire Permag enterprise.

  

##### **Major Responsibilities - reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions:**

  

**Division Functions**

**Customer Quality & Strategic Relationships**

* Establish a customer-focused Quality culture throughout the Division.
* Provide leadership for significant customer quality issues, escalations, complaints, corrective actions, and recovery plans in the Division.
* Partner with Commercial and Operations leadership to protect and strengthen key customer relationships.
* Identify systemic customer quality trends and ensure corrective actions address root causes rather than symptoms.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Operational Quality & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive measurable improvements in first-pass yield, scrap, rework, nonconforming material, customer complaints, warranty/returns, CAPA effectiveness, and cost of poor quality.
* Establish Division Quality KPIs and performance expectations.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to eliminate systemic process variation and improve manufacturing capability.
* Champion prevention-based Quality and continuous improvement methodologies throughout the Division
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Quality Organization & Talent**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Division Quality organization.
* Establish organizational structure, roles, competencies, and succession plans necessary to support the Division’s current operations and future growth.
* Develop Quality leaders and technical talent through coaching, mentoring, and targeted development.
* Establish clear accountability and performance expectations across the Quality organization.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Risk Management**

* Identify and proactively manage Division Quality risks that could impact customers, operations, financial performance, reputation, or business continuity.
* Establish escalation protocols for significant Quality risks and provide leadership with timely visibility and recommendations.
* Partner with leadership to assess Quality risks associated with new customers, products, technologies, suppliers, facilities, and acquisitions.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**New Product & Business Growth**

* Ensure Quality is embedded into new product development, design transfer, manufacturing process development, and launch activities.
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to establish appropriate quality controls prior to production launch.
* Provide Quality leadership and due diligence support for acquisitions, integrations, new facilities, and significant business expansion.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

**Leadership & Governance**

* Serve as a member of the Division leadership team and provide insight regarding Quality performance, risks, trends, and opportunities.
* Establish regular Quality performance reviews with executive and site leadership.
* Present enterprise Quality performance, significant risks, customer issues, and strategic initiatives to Division and upon request to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Influence organizational decisions through data-driven analysis, sound business judgment, and a strong understanding of customer and operational requirements.
* Support these activities outside the Division upon request.

  

**Permag Enterprise Functions**

**Enterprise Quality Strategy**

* Coordinate the development and execution of Permag’s long-term Quality strategy aligned with business objectives, growth plans, customer requirements, and operational priorities.
* Coordinate the establishment of enterprise-wide Quality objectives, policies, standards, KPIs, and governance.
* Provide input into strategic planning, capital investment, new product development, operational expansion, and business growth initiatives relative to the Quality Function.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Ensure coordination of Permag’s Quality Management Systems across all locations.
* Coordinate consistent enterprise-wide processes for audits, CAPA, nonconforming material, corrective action, change control, document control, and quality risk management.
* Maintain organizational readiness for customer, regulatory, and third-party audits.
* Serve as the executive authority for and quality-related regulatory actions.

  

Other duties and projects assigned.

  

**Qualifications**

**Education, Experience & Certifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering required; advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in Quality within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience leading Quality organizations across multiple manufacturing sites and/or business units.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise-wide Quality strategies.
* Extensive experience with ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, and applicable regulatory/customer requirements.
* Experience with ITAR and export-control compliance preferred.
* Lead Auditor certification strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience working directly with executive leadership and major customers.
* Experience leading organizational transformation, continuous improvement, and cultural change.
* This position may require access to ITAR-controlled technical data and services. As such, all applicants must be U.S. persons, as defined by ITAR, to be considered for this role. A U.S. person is a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or individual with protected status under U.S. immigration laws. Applicants who do not meet these criteria will not be considered for the position

  

Salary Range: $220,000-$235,000 + bonus

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including Medical/Rx, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts, Basic Life/AD&D (includes coverage for dependents 100% Company paid), Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability (100% Company paid), Supplemental Life/AD&D, 401(k) with Company match, tuition assistance after 1 year, paid time off, and 11 paid holidays.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities

Join a company where innovation drives growth. At Alloy Precision Technologies, we combine cutting-edge manufacturing, skilled craftsmanship, and a customer-first mindset to deliver industry-leading solutions while providing employees opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

Alloy Precision Technologies

  

**SUMMARY:**

To provide strategic, operational, and day-to-day leadership to the manufacturing operations and manufacturing services function at Alloy Precision Technologies (APT) and to grow the business by increased productivity and profitability within a lean environment. Must be a proven leader who is capable of dealing with sometimes complex and difficult situations.

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Leads performance in the planning, coordination, and control of all manufacturing, supply chain, maintenance, production planning, and warehouse functions at APT and the personnel assigned to those functions.
* Establish both quality and efficiency in all production processes to meet performance objectives.
* Promote positive leadership to ensure safety goals and environmental programs for manufacturing operations.
* Direct, monitor, and provide specific feedback on production issues, opportunities, and delays. This will require a proactive approach to investigation and analysis, troubleshooting, and resolution.
* Design and implement on-time tracking systems to monitor manufacturing schedules and operations as necessary to ensure profitability, timely service, and product quality for strong customer service. Provide reports as requested or needed on all aspects of the manufacturing operation.
* Lead the development and implementation of improved operating methods via lean or other strategic manufacturing flow and business process systems and procedures to reduce costs, improve quality performance, and improve profitability.
* Develop effective lines of communication and cooperation between corporate departments and functions within areas of responsibility.
* Promote strong team-building skills. Demonstrate ability to mentor and motivate, as well as to delegate and empower others to succeed.
* Formulate annual operational objectives and programs governing manufacturing, service, and distribution.
* Performs described duties to meet or exceed Customer, AS9100, and regulatory requirements.
* Domestic and international travel may be required.
* Performs other duties assigned by the President and Chief Executive Officer.

  

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Directly supervises group leaders, supply chain, and production planning. Direct reports may be added or subtracted over time.
* Incumbent will carry out supervisory and managerial responsibilities by following APT organizational policies, applicable federal, state, and local laws. Responsibilities include: interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance: rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints, resolving problems, and career development.

  

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* BS in Operations Management, Industrial Management, Industrial Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with 10 plus years of manufacturing management experience. Experience in precision welding (tig, laser, brazing, and soldering), CNC and manual machining, and light assembly operations is a plus.
* Incumbent must have strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications. Experience with computer database systems, Visual Manufacturing, and the development of labor standards for cost structure is a plus. Must have a high level of energy, be results-oriented, confident, and have strong people skills. Must be able to establish and maintain a strong rapport and positive relationships with all levels of staff. Must be strategic in his/her orientation, proactive, persistent, and able to handle multiple projects and customers simultaneously, as well as work within a very fast-paced environment.
* Because the company runs at a very fast pace with multiple, rapidly changing priorities, the incumbent must be highly flexible, resilient, adaptable, and comfortable working in a dynamic organization with an evolving culture. Incumbent must enjoy a challenge, be passionate about his/her work, and commit to excellence and continuous improvement.
* Working knowledge of lean manufacturing methodologies required, Six Sigma is a plus.

protected_roles.description:
**About Site**
--------------

Catalent’s Greendale, Indiana site is a key part of the company’s Wellness business, serving as one of North America’s primary gummy development and manufacturing centers. The site specializes in the formulation and production of traditional gelatin gummies and 100% plant‑based pectin gummies for nutritional supplements and nutraceutical applications, supporting a wide range of consumer health products. With strong in‑house R&D, quality laboratories, and flexible manufacturing and packaging capabilities, the Greendale operation partners closely with customers to develop innovative, high‑quality, and consumer‑friendly gummy delivery formats across a variety of flavors, shapes, and functional ingredients, all produced under rigorous quality and food‑safety standards.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager, Quality Systems to join our team and lead the Quality and Compliance functions at the Catalent Greendale site. This role oversees a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and release. The position ensures compliance with industry standards and regulations while driving continuous improvement across the Quality organization. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross‑functional teams to maintain product integrity and ensure the consistent delivery of high‑quality products to our customers.

Shift: Monday through Friday, 8:00AM - 5:00PM  
Location: Greendale, IN  
100% Onsite

**The Role**
------------

* Oversee Quality and Compliance functions related to dietary supplement manufacturing at the Catalent Greendale site.
* Lead a team of Quality Assurance Supervisors and Specialists responsible for operational quality, product sampling, testing, and product release.
* Review and approve manufacturing and packaging change controls, product formulations, label changes, deviations, corrective and preventive action plans, and customer complaints.
* Ensure compliance with FDA, NSF, and SQF requirements for product manufacturing and participate in internal and external audits.
* Develop and maintain quality and compliance policies, procedures, and guidelines.
* Identify and mitigate risks related to product quality and oversee root cause analyses and corrective actions.
* Lead the Food Safety Team and ensure compliance with 21 CFR 110 and 117, HACCP Food Safety, and Food Defense Plans.
* Monitor the sanitary state of the facility and equipment to ensure cross‑contamination control.
* Collaborate with Operations to assess the effectiveness of sanitation programs and ensure compliance with food safety guidelines.
* Maintain a feedback loop with Customer Service to address quality issues affecting product release.
* Oversee training programs to educate staff on quality standards and compliance requirements.
* Establish and track key performance indicators to measure quality and compliance performance.
* Collaborate with Product Development, Technical Operations, and Supply Chain teams to integrate quality into all production processes.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency.
* Communicate effectively with regulatory agencies, external auditors, and internal stakeholders on quality and compliance matters.
* Oversee investigations, environmental monitoring, and critical control point incidents impacting product release.
* Support site management in enforcing current Good Manufacturing Practices and mentoring staff in compliance.
* Facilitate internal assessments, compliance meetings, and training sessions.

**The Candidate**
-----------------

### **Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in science or related field (Chemistry, Microbiology, or Biology) and at least five years of pharmaceutical and dietary supplement quality experience.
* Minimum of seven years of related experience, including three to four years in a supervisory or management role.
* Experience in current Good Manufacturing Practice compliance and working in a quality role within the pharmaceutical or dietary supplement manufacturing industry.
* Ability to work effectively under pressure to meet deadlines. The individual may be required to sit, stand, walk regularly, and occasionally lift up to 15 pounds; no lifting greater than 44.09 pounds without assistance. Must be accessible to the manufacturing floor and office staff and use required office equipment. Specific vision requirements include reading written documents and frequent use of a computer monitor.
* Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent‑sponsored leadership programs such as NGGL, GOLD, LEAD Now, GM Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience.

### **Preferred Skills & Background**

* Experience with investigation writing, including root cause analysis and report preparation for annual product reviews.
* Familiarity with regulations 21 CFR 111, 21 CFR 117, 21 CFR 211, GFSI, HACCP, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual, SQF, NSF, and UL certifications.
* Experience with electronic systems such as JDE, TrackWise, Electronic Document Management System, Learning Management System, Quality Management System, Veeva, Compliance Wire, and Stability Programs.
* Experience communicating with FDA inspectors or other regulatory agents and handling FDA 483 responses.
* Experience using artificial intelligence tools to improve quality systems.

**Why You Should Join Catalent**
--------------------------------

* Positive and fast‑paced working environment focusing on continually improving processes to remain innovative and dynamic.
* Competitive Paid Time Off plus eight paid holidays.
* Medical, dental, and vision benefits effective day one of employment.
* Tuition Reimbursement – support to complete or earn a new degree.
* Site‑based Employee Engagement activities such as End‑of‑Summer and NFL kickoff celebrations, March Madness tournament, Summer Food Truck Fridays, Veterans Appreciation Lunch, Homemade Chili Cook‑off, Salsa Competition, Ice Cream Sundae Bar, and more.
* Employee Resource Groups focusing on Diversity and Inclusion.
* Environmentally friendly, community engagement green initiatives.
* Defined career path and annual performance review process with potential for career growth on an expanding team.
* WellHub program promoting overall physical and mental wellness.
* Perkspot offering exclusive discounts from over 900 merchants across various categories.

**Catalent offers rewarding opportunities to further your career!** Join the global drug development and delivery leader and help us bring over 7,000 life-saving and life-enhancing products to patients around the world. Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking a Senior Manager, External Manufacturing (Operations Lead) to drive day-to-day execution, operational readiness, and world-class performance across our Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) network while leading a team focused on continuous improvement and technical excellence.

  
  

**When & where:**

* Location: East Greenbush, NY
* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
* Travel requirement: 25-50%
  

  

**Discover your role:**

* Ensures product manufacture occurs in compliance with cGMP and applicable regulations.
* Facilitates all External Manufacturing activities at CMO/partner sites: batch scheduling, supply of materials, direct shipment, cycle time tracking, reports and technical expertise.
* Ensures, in collaboration with EM Project Management, timely routing/review of technical transfer activities, validation plans, MRs, SOPs, and other documentation.
* Implements site initiatives in production operation as directed by site management.
* Leads continuous improvements, system implementations and/or strategy development to reduce cycle times and improve efficiency for area.
* Ensures off-site inspections, testing and shipping/packaging is done according to guidelines and specifications.
* Ensures product integrity and company reputation by assisting in the monitoring of cGMP compliance at contract manufacturers.
* Supports investigations which concern External Manufacturing or associated shipping operations, as required.
* Manages direct reports and/or lead a sub-team in continuous process improvements, system/equipment implementation and/or strategy development.
* Assists in developing metrics to analyze department activities, workload and performance.
* Maintains required training status on Regeneron specific work instructions and SOPs.
  

  

**This role requires:**

* BS/BA in business or scientific discipline and 8 years of related experience, including a minimum of 5 years of direct cGMP manufacturing operations experience (clinical and/or commercial); remaining years may be satisfied through supplier management experience or equivalent combination of education and experience. MBA preferred.

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

  
  

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

  
  

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

$126,300.00 - $206,100.00

protected_roles.title: Senior Manager Quality Operations
protected_roles.description:
**Job Description:**
--------------------

As a privately-owned, biopharmaceutical company, Ferring pioneers and delivers life-changing therapies that help people build families and live better lives. Our independence helps us cultivate an entrepreneurial spirit and long-term perspective that enables us to achieve growth and scale, while remaining agile and true to our ‘people first’ philosophy. Built on a 70-year plus commitment to science and research, Ferring is relentless in its pursuit of science that drives powerful discoveries and therapies to help people build families, stay healthy, and stand up to the world’s oldest enemy: disease.

  

**Summary:** The Sr. Quality Operations Manager is responsible for establishing and maintaining Quality Operations systems to support and provide quality oversight to Manufacturing Operations, Technical Services, Donor Management program, Supply Chain and R&D areas for Clinical and Commercially distributed products. This position is responsible for managing a team to meet product demand requirements and timelines by supporting manufacturing activities including: Donor and Material Hold program, issuance of batch records, in-process Quality review, review of analytical data and batch records and final disposition of product with a complex set of requirements and controls, in accordance with GXP regulations. This role will also work with partners in the development of new Clinical products and programs, with integration activities to support objectives.

With Ferring, you will be joining a recognized leader, identified as one of “The World’s Most Innovative Companies” by Fast Company, and honored by Fortune with inclusion on its “Change the World List,” for addressing society’s unmet needs. Ferring US is also Great Places to Work® Certified, distinguishing it as one of the best companies to work for in the country.

**Responsibilities:**

**Lead the Management of Quality Operations Functions:**

* Manage the batch record issuance, batch record review, analytical testing review, COA creation, and disposition processes according to product requirements. This may include both Commercial and Phase I, II or III
* Manage and maintain the Donor and Material Hold program to ensure Quality oversight and control of donors and materials.
* Manage the collection and reporting of records via paper and electronic systems to support timely review and retrieval.
* Manage the incoming inspection of raw materials and components.
* Manage the COA creation and submission process per product and regulatory requirements.
* Establish and maintain the lot release schedule to meet customer and site demands.
* Perform technical investigations relating to site deviations, customer complaints and other areas as needed.
* Identify, establish and support operational initiatives to improve compliance and right-first-time execution.
* Establish metrics and provide trend information for KPI and Metrics reporting systems, including management review and annual product reviews.
* Establish the Quality Operations Systems to assure robust design to meet cGMP requirements to prevent or reduce human error, including electronic system design and implementation
* undefined

**Perform label approval and disposition finished product during shipping operations.**

* Perform label approval for intermediate, bulk and finished product.
* Perform real-time review of labeled, packaged finished product, and perform disposition during shipping operations to support commercial markets and Clinical trials.
Evaluate finished product labeling and batch record requirements for commercial or clinical trial markets in US or global.  

  

**Provide support to R&D manufacturing teams from Phase 1 to Phase 3 development to commercialization, according to cGMP.**·

* Support creation of Master Batch Records, specifications, COAs, and release criteria.
* Manage the process to support batch review, including CMO records, including all testing requirements and Certificate of Analysis program, and perform final disposition.
* Support process validation and technology transfer activities, including creation and review of associated batch documentation
* Support the development of processes and systems during manufacturing or distribution activities by a CMO to support pharmaceutical development and manufacturing.

**Provide Quality System and Regulatory Support as needed, related to:**

* Investigational Systems (Product Complaint, Deviations, CAPAs, OOS).
* Audit Preparedness and Back Room functions.CMC/IND/BLA writing and/or reviewing.
* Represent QOPs on cross-functional projects teams, with Ferring colleagues in multiple geographies.

**Hire, manage and develop direct reports**·

* Plan staffing levels. Recruit, interview, select, hire, and employ an appropriate number of employees
* Coach, mentor and develop staff, including overseeing new employee onboarding and providing career development planning and opportunities
* Lead employees to meet the organization's expectations for productivity, quality, and goal accomplishment
* Provide effective performance feedback through employee recognition, rewards, and disciplinary action when necessary
* Provide effective performance feedback through employee recognition, rewards, and disciplinary action when necessary.

**Any other duties as assigned for business reasons**.

**Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific field (preferably in Microbiology), Advanced degree preferred.
* Seven or more years of management experience.
* Seven or more years of experience in an FDA regulated manufacturing environment with Quality Assurance experience for medical products.
* At least three of these years in a pharmaceutical and/or biopharmaceutical environment.
* Knowledge of quality regulations and current industry practices.
* In-depth knowledge of 21 CFR 210 & 211 GMP regulations.
* Preferred knowledge of 21 CFR 600 & 610 GMP regulations.
* Preferred knowledge of 21 CRR 820 and ISO 13485.

**Ferring + you**

At Ferring, we offer competitive total compensation along with an exceptional range of flexible benefits, personal support and tailored learning and development opportunities all designed to help you realize your full potential both in life and at work. From working hours that respect your lifestyle, a culture that is welcoming and equitable, and the chance to work with the industry’s most impressive people, these are just some of the ways we live our "People First" philosophy.

  

**Our Compensation and Benefits**

At Ferring, base salary is one part of our competitive total compensation and benefits package and is determined using a salary range. The base salary range for this role is $121,299 to $173,284, which is the reasonable estimate of the base compensation for this role. The actual amount paid may differ based on non-discriminatory factors such as experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, education and primary work location. Additional compensation for this role will be provided based on competitive annual incentive compensation targets in the form of an annual bonus - payouts are based on individual and company performance.Benefits for this role include comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, and vision) with a premium differential, inverse to base salary, to be paid by employees, a 401k plan and company match, short and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, wellness benefits, reimbursement for certain tuition expenses, sick time of 1 hour per 30 hours worked, vacation time for full time employees to accrue up to 120 hours in the first four (4) years of employment, and 160 hours in the fifth (5th) year of employment as well as 15 paid holidays per year. We are proud to offer paid parental leave subject to a minimum period of employment at Ferring. Ferring is an equal opportunity employer.

  

All aspects of employment will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local laws.

  

Join our team and your voice will be heard, and your contributions will be valued. If you love to come up with new ways to make a positive difference and see them through, you will fit right in.

  

We are proud to be an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer (including Disability/Protected Veterans). We maintain a drug-free workplace.

protected_roles.description:
**Job Title:**

Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering (Burnet, TX)

**Job Description:**

**THE ROLE**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality Engineering is responsible for leading manufacturing quality across two Entegris manufacturing sites in Texas and translating global quality standards and quality priorities into consistent site execution. This role provides multi-site leadership to reduce risk, strengthen process capability, improve customer satisfaction, and deliver measurable quality improvements across the two-site footprint.  
  
The Senior Manager partners with site Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Customer Quality, Product Quality and Quality Systems teams to embed quality ownership into daily operations. This leader is accountable for site quality performance, consistent implementation of quality standards, compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and customer requirements, and the development of capable site quality teams. The role leads through site quality leaders and teams, establishes clear ownership and follow-through, and escalates risks and resource needs to North America quality leadership.

The hired individual will work on-site at our Burnet, TX location with some travel to our Decatur, TX location.

  

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* Translate global quality standards and quality priorities into coordinated execution plans for the two Texas sites, with clear owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
* Lead manufacturing quality across all two sites through site quality leaders and teams; clarify responsibilities, prioritize resources based on risk, and maintain regular on-site engagement.
* Ensure consistent implementation of global quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices; maintain audit readiness and timely closure of findings at each site.
* Partner with site Operations leaders to establish quality roadmaps, objectives, and common key performance indicators (KPIs); conduct routine cross-site reviews and drive recovery plans where performance falls short.
* Own quality improvement plans that reduce defects, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality (COPQ), customer complaints, and manufacturing escapes, with site-level accountability for results.
* Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve process capability, product conformity, yield, and manufacturing performance through effective process controls and proactive risk management.
* Lead targeted continuous improvement and change implementation across the two sites; standardize effective practices and verify that improvements are sustained.
* Ensure timely containment, disciplined root cause analysis, corrective/preventive action, and effectiveness verification for significant quality issues; deploy lessons learned across all two sites.
* Ensure practical, sustained application of SPC, MSA, FMEA, control plans, APQP, PPAP, 8D, A3, and DMAIC methodologies, as applicable to site processes and customer requirements.
* Serve as the quality escalation leader for the two Texas sites; communicate risk, containment status, recovery plans, and decisions needed, and escalate significant issues to Quality leadership.
* Partner with Customer Quality and Product Quality teams to resolve customer issues through timely, evidence-based investigations, effective corrective actions, and proactive communication.
* Develop site quality leaders and teams through coaching, clear expectations, technical capability building, and succession planning; identify staffing and resource needs across the two sites.
* Foster shared quality ownership across functions, reinforce accountability for commitments, and promote collaboration and continuous improvement across the two sites.
* Travel requirements will be a minimum of 25%, including regular presence across the two Texas sites.

**WHAT WE SEEK**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related field required.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing quality, including leadership responsibility for quality teams and manufacturing quality outcomes.
* 5+ years of quality management experience, with demonstrated ability to lead through site leaders or cross-functional teams; multi-site leadership experience preferred.
* Demonstrated success implementing quality systems and delivering sustained improvements in manufacturing quality, process capability, and cost of poor quality.
* Ability to coordinate priorities, standardize practices, and maintain effective leadership presence across two manufacturing sites in Texas.
* Experience supporting customer and supplier quality requirements, audit readiness, and compliance with applicable regulatory and industry requirements.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence site leaders, resolve competing priorities, and communicate risks and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Demonstrated experience coaching quality leaders, developing technical capability, and building team depth and succession readiness across sites.
* Demonstrated ability to lead practical change, establish clear ownership, and sustain common quality practices in partnership with Operations and Engineering.
* Strong problem-solving, data analysis, and business acumen, with practical application of quality tools to prioritize risk, improve manufacturing processes, and deliver measurable results.

**WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS?**  
Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future.  
  
Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office.

**WHAT WE OFFER**  
Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals.

* Compensation: The salary range for this position is $134,000- $196,500 per year. Final compensation will depend on the candidate's overall skills and qualifications for the role.
* Annual bonus eligibility
* Progressive paid time off policy that empowers you to take the time you need to recharge
* Generous 401(K) plan with an impressive employer match with no delayed vesting
* Excellent health, dental and vision insurance packages to fit your needs
* Education assistance to support your learning journey
* A values-driven culture with colleagues that rally around People, Accountability, Creativity and Excellence

*Entegris does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need Entegris immigration sponsorship (e.g., H1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) now or in the future.*

*At Entegris we are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and applicants. Our policy is to recruit, hire, train, and reward employees for their individual abilities, achievements, and experience without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, marital or military status.*

protected_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality Systems and Compliance
protected_roles.description:
Apnimed is a rapidly growing pharmaceutical company working to transform the treatment of sleep apnea based on a simple idea – patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) could benefit from treatment with a safe and effective oral medication dosed once daily at bedtime. Our lead development program, AD109, targets the neurologic control of upper airway muscles to maintain an open airway during sleep. Apnimed is committed to innovation, as well as state-of-the-art advancements in sleep medicine, which is leading to the development of a portfolio of novel pharmacologic therapies for sleep apnea and related disorders.

Recognized by the Boston Business Journal as one of the Best Places to Work in both 2024 and 2025, we are continuing to grow and build the foundational operations that enable our employees and our mission to thrive.

**Summary**:

The Senior Manager, Quality Systems & Compliance reports to the Senior Director, GCP Quality Assurance and Quality Compliance and is responsible for administering, maintaining, and continuously improving Apnimed's electronic Quality Management System (eQMS) and associated quality processes, and for keeping them inspection-ready. The successful candidate will also play a key role in strengthening the Quality Management System infrastructure as a business partner across GxP and corporate quality functions, ensuring quality processes remain compliant, scalable, and aligned with the company's transition toward commercialization. This is an exciting opportunity to strengthen the quality infrastructure that supports Apnimed as part of a major paradigm shift in the treatment of sleep apnea from medical devices and surgery to a first in class pharmaceutical treatment.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is $170,000.00 to $190,000.00. Final compensation will depend on the selected candidate’s level, education and relevant experience.

### **Key Job Duties include, but are not limited to:**

* Serve as subject matter expert and administrator for the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), evaluating proposed system changes and coordinating testing, validation, and deployment activities.
* Support the integration of new business processes, departments, and vendors into the Quality Management System, and oversee onboarding, knowledge transfer, and competency requirements for new eQMS administrators.
* Maintain system documentation, including procedures, work instructions, validation documentation, and configuration records.
* Administer the training program: confirm assignments and curricula reflect quality system responsibilities, manage role-based eQMS training and user support, and maintain a centralized library of user guidance, job aids, and FAQs.
* Provide oversight and support for core quality processes, including document control, deviations, CAPAs, change controls, investigations, supplier quality records, and training management.
* Manage vendor governance activities and periodic performance reviews, ensuring reviews are completed and properly documented and filed.
* Keep quality systems and records in a state of continuous inspection readiness; support regulatory inspections and audits through preparation of records, reports, metrics, and system demonstrations; and monitor industry trends and regulatory expectations.
* Present quality system performance trends and recommendations to Quality leadership, lead or support continuous improvement initiatives, and collaborate cross-functionally to standardize quality processes across departments.

  
**Requirements**  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent in a scientific, technical, engineering, quality, or related discipline.
* 8+ years of Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, or Quality Management experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences industry, including:
* Demonstrated experience managing electronic Quality Management Systems (eQMS), including administering or supporting platforms such as Dot Compliance, Veeva Quality, MasterControl, TrackWise Digital, ComplianceWire, or similar.
* Working knowledge of FDA, EMA, ICH, GCP, GMP, and GLP requirements.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and external/internal audits.
* Preferred: Direct administrator experience with Veeva Quality, and experience with computerized system validation (CSV) and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.
* Preferred: Experience supporting both development-stage and commercial pharmaceutical operations, and implementing or enhancing eQMS platforms.
* Ability to manage simultaneous priorities and changing deadlines.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills.
* Proficiency in the use of MS Word, PowerPoint; experience with Adobe Acrobat Professional.

  
**Benefits**  

* 401(k) with company match
* Generous time off for vacation
* Generous healthcare benefits
* Flexible working environment
* Motivated and experienced team
* Winner of 2024 and 2025 Boston Business Journal Best Places to Work

### **Location and Other Information:**

* Apnimed is a publicly licensed company based in Cambridge, MA; we are generally virtual and specific location within the US is not critical.
* We are a small growing Company with an inclusive environment.
* Must be able to travel as necessary.
* Apnimed is an EEO employer committed to an exciting, diverse, and enriching work environment.
* Please visit us at www.apnimed.com to learn more about our work with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

**Company Description**

With over $2B in revenue, 80+ manufacturing facilities across 6 continents and over 9,000 employees worldwide, Signode is a leading manufacturer of a broad spectrum of transit packaging consumables, tools, software, and equipment that optimize end-of-line packaging operations and protect products in transit. Signode brings this extensive product portfolio together under hundreds of trusted brands to offer complete transit packaging solutions to its customers.  
  
We produce strap, stretch and protective packaging. We also manufacture packaging tools and equipment used to apply the bulk packaging materials. These commercial packaging products are used to pack, bundle, unitize, protect, and secure goods during warehousing and transit. Our company is a pioneer in the industrial packaging sector with a long history of customer-focused innovations in materials, processes and automation technology that have revolutionized the sector.  
  
Headquartered in Tampa, Florida, we are proud to be the Transit Packaging Division of Crown Holdings, Inc. We are excited to go to market as Signode and to share the portfolio of products, services and capabilities that make us the world’s premier end-of-line packaging company.

 **Job Description**

Signode offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees, which includes health, dental, vision, 401k, paid time off, life insurance, wellness perks, and more. Benefits begin the month following the hire date.

The position calls for a sharp operational and analytical mind that constantly seeks out, teaches, and leads improvements in Safety Performance, Cost Control, Standardized Processes (LEAN), Production Reporting, and Inventory Control.

This is a high-visibility opportunity to lead one of Signode’s most important locations, having a big impact on our ability to deliver a profitable year. Here is what makes this role stand out:

* Pilot the company’s Operational Excellence system, delivering a glidepath in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Output, and Morale.

* Lead and support initiatives for continuous improvement, identifying opportunities to enhance plant processes, reduce waste, and increase overall efficiency.

  
**Qualifications**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Management, Business, or Engineering. Masters Degree in similar field preferred.

**Experience:** Minimum of 15+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, with at least 5 -7 years in a managerial or supervisory role. **Previous experience as a plant manager is a must.**

**Functional Success Drivers:** These competencies are what we require for an individual to be successful in this role.

protected_roles.title: Director, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.

* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
